subject: Promote
claim: Promote and Demote let one player move a rival's members, which wrecks member plans and is the only way a small cult touches the Red and Yellow contests.
evidence: Four swaps aimed at rival cults (Clan, Dabblers, Loyalists, Spoilsport) moved roughly 25 contest followers, all off Ava, and Ava left both spaces open on her round III double turn.

subject: Demote
claim: Demote and Promote give a lean cult real levers on the leader and create the game's biggest swings.
evidence: Ben's Demote took Clan off Ava before it paid (about 6 to 8 followers) and his round III Demote took Spoilsport, the move that won 87 to 86.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Spoilsport cancels a contest after the last placement and can decide a close game with no reply.
evidence: Ben cancelled the 3-3 Yellow tie, taking 5 from Ava who lost by 1; without it Ava wins 91 to 87.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Holding the veto into the last round end is the tensest decision of the game.
evidence: Ben's choice between Red and Yellow at round III end decided the winner.

subject: Fewest members
claim: One small cult wins Fewest members every round with nobody contesting it.
evidence: Ben won it +4, +6, +10 with 1 to 2 members while the next-smallest cult had 2, 4 and 4.

subject: Modest Means
claim: Modest Means rewards the small cult directly for staying small.
evidence: It paid Ben +4 white twice (rounds II and III) because both rivals had more members.

subject: Buying followers
claim: Once members stop paying back, the recruit step becomes the same follower buy every turn.
evidence: 23 of 36 recruit steps were follower buys; Ben's last 10 of 12 recruits were 5-follower buys.

subject: White Cloak
claim: The White Cloak refunds part of every follower buy, making the buying line a loop that needs few decisions and outpaces the other cloaks.
evidence: The White Cloak paid 22 white over 11 buys, against 12 yellow for the Yellow Cloak and 7 red for the Red Cloak.

subject: Round end
claim: The last placement of the game can collapse into several options that all give +1 follower.
evidence: Ava reached her last turn with 0 resources after a 1-follower buy; Ben and Cal still had a 5- and a 10-follower buy.

subject: Patrons
claim: Giving a member away pays the giver its cost while the receiver gets a card they did not choose.
evidence: Ava's Patrons paid her +7 for Brokers; Guest of Honor paid her +4; the receivers got 1 printed follower each.

subject: Write-Off
claim: A gifted member can be passed on again, so a gift lands on a player its first giver never chose.
evidence: Ava gave Brokers to Cal for +7, Cal wrote it off to Ben for 8 white, and Ben's +1 printed follower was the winning margin.

subject: Write-Off
claim: Being given a member hurts the receiver in the Fewest members contest and leaves them with a useless card.
evidence: Cal had 6 members to Ben's 1 before Brokers arrived, so White did not change, and he turned Brokers into 8 white and a 10-follower buy.

subject: Round end
claim: A player out of the race decides the winner by choosing which leader receives a gift.
evidence: Cal's choice to write Brokers off to Ben instead of Ava gave Ben the 1 follower he won by.

subject: Dabblers
claim: Dabblers at 5 counts as 2 members of one color and adds a missing color, so it decides contests far above its price.
evidence: Free off Late Shift, it won Ava round I Red, round I Yellow outright and round II Red (about 12 followers), then gave Cal the Yellow tie in round III.

subject: Borrow
claim: It is unclear whether a borrowed member given to a rival still returns to the shop.
evidence: Borrow's text says the member returns at round end, and the log returned Guest of Honor from Ben's cult as printed; Ben had planned to use it every round.

subject: Makeover
claim: Makeover's rearrange does nothing when no contest counts resources.
evidence: Ben's last-turn Makeover rearrange was a confirmation click; none of White, Red or Yellow counts resources.

subject: Makeover
claim: Makeover reshaping the whole pile at once frees a player stuck with the wrong colors.
evidence: Cal turned his pile into 7 red to buy Brethren in round II.

subject: Body Snatchers
claim: Members with only a Round Start ability do nothing if bought in round III.
evidence: Cal's round III Body Snatchers never acted; he bought it for Gather's +4 and Brethren's +1.

subject: Loyalists
claim: Loyalists protects your other members but can be swapped away itself, which surprised a new player.
evidence: Ben's Promote swapped Cal's Loyalists out, then his Demote took Spoilsport; the text says 'your other members'.

subject: Cash In
claim: Cash In is a single center space, so it becomes denial, and its +1 white back is a crumb that needs a recruit.
evidence: Ava's Cash In turned 3 white into 5 followers (with Brokers) and left 1 white that became 1 follower for a whole recruit.

subject: Offering
claim: Offering feeds your buy and taxes both rivals in one placement.
evidence: It gave Ava 5 yellow for a 5-follower buy and made Ben discard 2 white and Cal 2 red.

subject: Late Shift
claim: Late Shift's limit growing with each minion placed makes the order of placements matter.
evidence: Ava's last-minion Late Shifts took Dabblers, Clan and Patrons free, worth 20 resources by price.

subject: Splurge
claim: Splurge's round II rate turns a member purchase into a big follower payout.
evidence: Splurge paid Ava +7 on Brokers in round II and Ben +3 on Anchorites in round I.

subject: New Blood
claim: New Blood with the Yellow Cloak refunds a first new-color member almost entirely, making the wide opening rewarding but nearly free.
evidence: Early Traders cost Ava 5 yellow and New Blood plus the cloak returned 5 the same turn.

subject: Early Traders
claim: Early Traders' Round Start swap turns a pile into an exact colored cost each round.
evidence: Ava swapped 3 yellow into white at round II start and paid exactly 7 for Brokers.

subject: Farewell
claim: Farewell and Patrons make round III a satisfying cash-out of finished members.
evidence: Farewell on Alchemists paid 9 and Patrons on Brokers paid 7 in Ava's round III.

subject: Turn order
claim: Back-to-back turns from the snake order let a player plan two-turn combos.
evidence: Cal's Write-Off, 1-follower buy, Nest Egg and 10-follower buy finish came from one double turn.

subject: Survey
claim: Survey's payout depends on where others crowded, a small reading puzzle.
evidence: Survey paid Ben 3, 4 and 5 yellow across the three rounds.

subject: Consolation Prize
claim: Consolation Prize pays a player who is losing contests and feels sweet and sour.
evidence: It paid Cal 10 followers for 7 resources, the best return on a bought member after Anchorites.

subject: Anchorites
claim: Anchorites pays +5 a round for 6 resources and is the best bought member for a small cult.
evidence: +3 from Splurge on the buy, +10 over two rounds, then traded for Spoilsport.

subject: Gather
claim: Gather's +4 followers cannot fire on a player's first member.
evidence: Cal's first-turn Gather into Loyalists paid no +4 because he had no color yet.

subject: Brethren
claim: Brethren pays less than a 5-follower buy over a game.
evidence: It cost Cal 7 and paid 3 followers plus 1 printed.

subject: Protesters
claim: Protesters' block comes too late in the turn order to be worth 6 resources.
evidence: Nobody paid for Protesters; its one appearance came free off Borrow and was never used.

subject: Most members of one color
claim: The contest text says each card counts 1, but Dabblers counts as 2 in the count.
evidence: Ava's round I count was 3 from Early Traders and Dabblers; Cal skipped Dabblers at [13] because of the printed text.

subject: Most member colors
claim: With three colors on the table the contest caps at 3, so ties at the cap are easy.
evidence: Round III was a 3-3 tie between Ava and Cal, which is what Spoilsport cancelled.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: A cult of 2 members won the game.
evidence: Ben won 87 to 86 holding 2 members, on 51 bought followers, 20 from Fewest members and 10 from Anchorites.

subject: Round end
claim: All round III contest followers moved through swaps and a veto, and the leader at round III start got none of them.
evidence: Ava led Red 4-3 and Yellow 3-1 at round III start and scored 0 of 30; Cal took Red +10 and Ben Fewest members +10.

subject: Turn order
claim: Fewest-followers-first order gave the leader's double turn before the swap player, and she did not use it to take the swap spaces.
evidence: Round III order was Cal, Ben, Ava; Ava took Cash In and Offering while Promote and Demote stayed open for Ben.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Members from free-recruit spaces paid as well as the best bought members.
evidence: Late Shift and Borrow gave 5 members worth 31 resources by price; Dabblers (about 12) and Patrons (7) matched Consolation Prize (10) and Purists (9).

subject: Buying followers
claim: No contest at this table counts resources, so every leftover goes into follower buys and color choices rarely matter.
evidence: Every pay-color choice in round III was called irrelevant by the payer; Makeover's rearrange and Early Traders' swap were called formalities.
